finding.claim: Unauthenticated remote code execution via unsafe deserialization: POST /restore passes an attacker-supplied, base64-encoded value directly to Marshal.load.
finding.source: app.rb:6 params[:state], a request parameter any unauthenticated client can set in the POST body.
finding.sink: app.rb:6 Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(...)). Ruby's Marshal format can instantiate arbitrary objects, and gadget chains in loaded gems can run code during deserialization.

trace.note: Route POST /restore is defined with no before-filter, auth check, or route condition.
params[:state] is read from the request and base64-decoded.
The decoded bytes are passed straight to Marshal.load, which deserializes attacker-controlled object graphs.
state.inspect runs on the result. This is reached only if loading does not already execute code.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization on the route. No HMAC or signature over the state blob to prove it was produced by the server. No Marshal allowlist (Marshal has no safe mode). No size limit on params[:state]. No type check that params[:state] is a String. Route is not behind a constraint or condition. No Rack middleware in app.rb that would filter the request. No other files in the directory to add a check elsewhere.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 defines POST /restore with no before-filter, auth, or route condition. app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight to Marshal.load with no signature, allowlist, size limit, or type check. app.rb:7 is state.inspect. The directory holds only app.rb, so no middleware or other file adds a control.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches app.rb:5-7, and the route at app.rb:5 is reachable anonymously and passes attacker-controlled bytes to Marshal.load at app.rb:6 with no effective control. The unauthenticated unsafe-deserialization flaw is confirmed. Reaching code execution specifically depends on gadget classes in the runtime gem set, which the directory (no Gemfile) cannot show, so the RCE severity is not fully verified, though the flaw itself is real.
